items.prompt:
A word specific to a field (like 'inflation') is a:
A) technical term
B) rhyme
C) title

The feeling a word carries beyond its meaning is its:
A) connotation
B) spelling
C) syllables

The overall effect built up by many word choices is their:
A) cumulative impact
B) page count
C) alphabetical order

Read.

Inflation, the sustained rise in prices, erodes purchasing power.

'Inflation' means:
A) falling prices
B) a sustained rise in prices
C) a type of tax
items.answer: B) a sustained rise in prices

steps: Defined in text. Key is B.
solution.answer: B) a sustained rise in prices

items.prompt:
Backers call a policy a 'reform'; critics call it a 'power grab.' These word choices:
A) steer readers toward opposite views via connotation
B) only affect spelling
C) change nothing
items.answer: A) steer readers toward opposite views via connotation

steps: Loaded words steer opinion. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) steer readers toward opposite views via connotation

items.prompt:
Why do informational authors DEFINE technical terms?
A) so readers understand field-specific vocabulary precisely
B) to pad the text
C) to confuse readers
items.answer: A) so readers understand field-specific vocabulary precisely

solution.answer: A) so readers understand field-specific vocabulary precisely

items.prompt:
Read.

The report calls the layoffs a 'streamlining,' an 'optimization,' and a 'right-sizing.'

The cumulative impact of these word choices is to:
A) soften and disguise the harm of the layoffs
B) describe them harshly
C) have no effect
items.answer: A) soften and disguise the harm of the layoffs

steps: Euphemisms build a softening effect. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) soften and disguise the harm of the layoffs

items.prompt:
An author repeatedly uses words like 'crisis,' 'collapse,' and 'catastrophe' about an issue. The cumulative tone is:
A) alarmed and urgent
B) calm and neutral
C) humorous

steps: Repeated alarming words. Key is A.
